And my second question is like Q1 had 11,497 camps and INR13.7 crores revenue, implying much higher revenue per camp than FY26.
And is it safe to assume that it's -- because these are a nnual contracts, so annual, say, expectation from PSP would be more like INR17.6 into 4, which i s around INR70-odd crores.
Growth & demand: Our consolidated revenues from the operations stood at INR56.9 cror es, registering a 22% year-on- year growth.
More importantly, our EBITDA grew faster than revenue, increasing 27% year on to INR8.3 crores with the EBITDA margin improving 14.6% compare d with 14.1% in Q1 FY '26 and 13.3% in the Q4 FY '26.
Quarter-on-quarter EBITDA grew by 41% and PAT more than doubled, increasing 110% over quarter 4 FY '26.
Margins & costs: While our PAT margins have improved to 7%, the sequential perf ormance is equally increasing.
So, we have a higher margin in camps and a lower margin in PSPs and the combined margins is what we estimate to be in 20% to 25% range.
You know, we had guided for 18%- odd EBITDA margin for FY '27.
Capex & expansion: So that is a driver for the expansion of gross margins.
There are certain -- this is a certain subset o f the product category which acquired PSP by default.
Balance sheet & cash: So, we were expecting some oper ating leverage coming from employee expenses.
So instead of operating leverage, we are seeing much more increased expenses.

The other thing which will help us to improve our leverage is, of course, as we mentioned earlier, is improving our services through our camps services with innovation in product services as well as the new products to improve the early diagnosis.
Risks & challenges: So, it will become -- an d as it has been in the past, an important asset for us as far as risk strategic initiative is concerned.

And you also mentioned that we'll have 2% EBITDA growth in FY27.
